title: Build Profiles
concept: Build profiles control optimization levels, debug info, and feature flags — debug for development, release for production, custom for specific needs.
why: Different stages need different builds. Debug builds need fast compilation and good diagnostics. Release builds need speed and small size. Profiles control this.
theory:
## Controlling Compilation

### Built-in Profiles

| Profile | Optimization | Debug Info | Contracts | Use Case |
|---------|-------------|------------|-----------|----------|
| `debug` | -O0 | Full | Checked | Development |
| `release` | -O3 | Stripped | Stripped | Production |
| `test` | -O0 | Full | Checked | Running tests |
| `bench` | -O3 | Minimal | Stripped | Benchmarking |

### Using Profiles

```sh
xiom build                          # Default: debug
xiom build --release                # Optimized for production
xiom build --profile test           # For running tests
xiom build --profile bench          # For benchmarking
```

### Custom Profiles

```toml
# xiom.toml
[profile.dev]
opt_level = 1          # Light optimization for faster debug builds
debug = true

[profile.release]
opt_level = 3          # Maximum optimization
lto = true             # Link-time optimization
codegen_units = 1      # Single codegen unit for better optimization
strip = true           # Strip debug symbols

[profile.custom_name]
opt_level = 2
debug = "limited"
contracts = "runtime"  # Keep contract checks even in optimized build
```

### Profile-Specific Code

```xiom
#[cfg(profile = "debug")]
fn expensive_debug_check(data: &Vec[Int]) {
  // Only runs in debug builds
}

#[cfg(profile = "release")]
fn expensive_debug_check(data: &Vec[Int]) {
  // Optimized away in release
}
```

### Optimization Levels

| Level | Compile Speed | Runtime Speed | Binary Size |
|-------|--------------|---------------|-------------|
| -O0 | Fast | Slow | Large |
| -O1 | Medium | Faster | Medium |
| -O2 | Slow | Fast | Medium |
| -O3 | Slowest | Fastest | Large |
| -Os | Medium | Fast | Small |
| -Oz | Slow | Moderately Fast | Smallest |
syntax_ref:
# Use a profile:
xiom build --release
xiom build --profile custom

# In xiom.toml:
[profile.custom]
opt_level = 2
debug = true
tips: Use `debug` profile during development — fastest compile times, best error messages
Use `release` profile for production — smaller binary, faster execution
Custom profiles let you balance: fast compilation with some optimization for integration tests
LTO (Link-Time Optimization) can significantly improve performance but slows compilation
common_mistakes: Profiling and benchmarking debug builds — always benchmark with release or bench profile
Using release profile in development — slow compile times kill productivity
Not defining custom profiles for special needs — reinventing flags every time
